data.description:
## Broken base: `/health` lifespan test asserts a stale exact dict (missing `queue_depth`)

`origin/main` HEAD is **red on CI** (ubuntu py3.12, wherever `fastapi` is installed) due to a
semantic conflict between two independently-landed Gerrit changes:

- `2bda965db6` (**9f63**) added `queue_depth` to the `/health` response body — intentional and
  documented (`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:274`):
  `return {"status": "ok", "in_flight": _voter.in_flight_reviews(), "queue_depth": queue_depth}`
- `4c89592d88` ("test: make review-bot lifespan safe") added
  `test_lifespan_is_safe_by_default_without_per_test_stubs`
  (`tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1449`) asserting **exact** equality:
  `assert response.json() == {"status": "ok", "in_flight": 0}` — missing `queue_depth`.

Each change passed `Verified +1` in isolation; Rebase-If-Necessary submitted them without
re-running the combined suite, so the merged tip fails. It skips locally when `fastapi` is
absent (why neither author caught it).

**This deterministically fails EVERY change's CI**, so it must be fixed on `main` before any
in-flight change (fc0c change 1528, etc.) can earn `Verified +1`.

### Fix
The endpoint's `queue_depth` key is intentional (bug 9f63); the test's exact-match assertion is
stale. Update the assertion to include the intentional key:
`assert response.json() == {"status": "ok", "in_flight": 0, "queue_depth": 0}`.

### Acceptance criteria
- AC1: `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py::test_lifespan_is_safe_by_default_without_per_test_stubs`
  passes with `fastapi` installed.
- AC2: The assertion accounts for all three intentional `/health` keys (`status`, `in_flight`,
  `queue_depth`) — no key dropped, no behavior changed in `app.py`.
- AC3: No other review-bot test regresses.
data.title: Fix stale /health lifespan test blocking all CI
